findings.evidence: `MellinConvergent f s := IntegrableOn (fun t => (t:ℂ)^(s-1) • f t) (Ioi 0)` (mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:45-46) versus `MellinDisConvergent` (Mellin.lean:95-97); the `←` direction is already proved at Strip.lean:128-130. With the iff, Mathlib's `hasMellin_cpow_Ioc` (MellinTransform.lean:453) gives the `→` half of `mellinDisConvergent_rpow_neg_iff` plus the value `1/(N-b)` directly.
findings.fix: State the iff publicly next to `mellinDis_eq_mellin_indicator` and derive `mellinDisConvergent_of_isBigO_rpow` from it. It is unconditional: the integrand `(t:ℂ)^(N-1) • indicator (Ioc 0 1) f t` vanishes on `Ioi 0 \ Ioc 0 1`, so `IntegrableOn _ (Ioi 0) ↔ IntegrableOn _ (Ioc 0 1)`, and on `Ioc 0 1` it is the `mellinDis` integrand.
findings.issue: The unconditional transfer `MellinDisConvergent f N ↔ MellinConvergent (fun x => (((Ioc 0 1).indicator f x : ℝ) : ℂ)) N` is never stated; only its `←` direction appears inline in `mellinDisConvergent_of_isBigO_rpow` (lines 128-130), specialized to the big-O hypothesis. A density whose small-`x` behaviour is not a pure-power `IsBigO` (exponential-type, or `x⁻¹ log(1/x)⁻²`) cannot reach convergence through the bridge at all and must redo the indicator argument.

findings.evidence: Strip.lean:96-105 derives `hloc` from `hf` alone; Strip.lean:107-111 derives `htop` from `eventually_gt_atTop 1` alone, with `N.re + 1` appearing only to match `hs_top : s.re < a` in `mellinConvergent_of_isBigO_rpow` (mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:277-279).
findings.fix: Promote them to public standalone lemmas: `LocallyIntegrableOn f (Ioc 0 1) → LocallyIntegrableOn (fun x => (((Ioc 0 1).indicator f x : ℝ) : ℂ)) (Ioi 0)`, and `(fun x => (((Ioc 0 1).indicator f x : ℝ) : ℂ)) =ᶠ[atTop] 0` (from which any `=O[atTop] (· ^ c)` follows). Keep the private lemma as the thin wiring, or drop it.
findings.issue: `hloc` (lines 96-105) and `htop` (lines 107-111) are general facts about the zero-extension that use none of the big-O data — `hloc` uses only `hf`, `htop` uses nothing about `f` — yet they are buried in a private lemma whose statement is specialized to one `N` and one `b`. These two are precisely the hypotheses every Mathlib `mellin` theorem demands (`hfc`, `hf_top`), so without them public, none of Mathlib's other Mellin results (`mellinConvergent_of_isBigO_rpow_exp`, `mellin_hasDerivAt_of_isBigO_rpow`, and the inversion material Layer 0.4 will need) can be applied to an interval density.

summary: Statements and hypotheses are at the right level throughout, but the file ships only half of the bridge it advertises: the value identity `mellinDis = mellin ∘ indicator` is public and unconditional, while the matching convergence identity and the reusable zero-extension lemmas are locked inside a private proof, so the only way to reach Mathlib's Mellin theory from `MellinDisConvergent` is through the two pre-packaged big-O corollaries.
